> Keep only a share of incoming traces to control storage and LLM scoring costs on a self-managed Weave instance

Ingest sampling lets you control the share of traces that arrive at a [self-managed Weave instance](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/platform/weave-self-managed.md) and drop the rest. search_evidence_for_optional_facts.snippet:
## Create a new signal

To start scoring your agent's turns, create one or more signals. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer.

The drawer groups available signals into two categories:

* **Tags**: Apply a label automatically to matching spans, such as `user-frustration` or `nsfw`. Use tags to categorize spans or flag unwanted behavior. The signals UI only displays rows for spans that matched at least one tag, so a tag signal might run successfully even if you don't see any output.
* **Ratings**: Assign a score from 0 to 1 to matching spans. Use ratings to rate agent performance and measure improvements over time.

# Score agent turns with a remote scorer

> Score Weave agent turns with your own HTTP endpoint and see the results as tags or ratings on the Signals tab.

A remote scorer signal scores each completed agent turn with an HTTP endpoint that you host, instead of with an LLM judge. When a turn ends, the Weave agent scoring worker sends the turn to your endpoint in an HTTP `POST` and records the response as feedback on the turn. The result appears as a tag or rating on the **Signals** tab of the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

This page covers remote scorers for agent turns. To score Calls traced with `@weave.op`, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md). You configure remote scorers with the Python SDK or the Weave UI. The TypeScript SDK doesn't include `RemoteScorer`.

documented_alternative.excerpt:
## Organize and compare evaluations

You improve an agent by changing its application and checking whether the change helped. The system prompt, the tools, the control flow, and the underlying LLM are all considered part of the model version. To compare two versions, run the evaluation again on the changed agent, labeled as a new version.

Re-run with a different `model` label:

```python lines highlight="4" theme={"system"}
# v2: the same tasks and loop, running a changed agent (e.g. a revised system prompt).
ev = weave.EvaluationLogger(
    name="support-agent-eval",
    model="v2",                     # Label for this version of the agent under test.
    dataset="support-refund-tasks",
)
# ... same loop as v1, running the changed agent ...
```

Weave lets you [Compare evaluations](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/compare_evals.md), so you can see whether v2 improved or regressed against v1 on the scores you logged, plus latency and cost.

observed_chronology.opening: **Short answer:** Weave scores a turn only after it ends, using a separate scoring worker [S2]. The docs I read don't say how long scoring takes or what latency the user sees. The user's answer comes from your agent code, and the scorer isn't described as a step inside that code. Scoring is triggered by the turn-ended event, so it can't be a prerequisite for finishing the turn.
observed_chronology.audit_issue: The sentence "Scoring is triggered by the turn-ended event, so it can't be a prerequisite for finishing the turn" is the answer's own inference, not stated in the docs. It follows from the sequence in S2 (root span ends, then the event). The docs say nothing about when the user actually receives the reply. The later hedge ("docs don't say whether your agent's reply waits") is the accurate framing, so the inference should be labelled as such.

observed_chronology.opening: **Short answer:** The docs don't say whether the user receives the answer before or after scoring finishes, so I can't give a definite yes or no. They describe scoring as starting once a turn has ended: a turn ends, Weave emits `weave.genai.turn_ended`, and a separate agent scoring worker then scores it [S2]. My inference, which the docs don't state, is that this makes scoring follow the turn and not run inside it. The docs also don't say how the reply timing relates to scoring.
